info.title: Monkeygun API
info.description: Data in, videos out. Every tool the Monkeygun studio has, over HTTP. Quote before you spend; paid calls return `charged`. 1 credit = $0.01. Docs: https://docs.monkeygun.com · MCP: npx @monkeygun/mcp

VideoStatus.description: draft → scripted (script, voice, images exist) → rendering → rendered, or error (see lastError)

Media.description: Keyed, absolute links — usable without a session. Present on every video response, on jobs (as `media`) and on webhooks.

renderUrl.description: This version's file (immutable, cache forever); null until rendered

video.description: Relative file path (needs a session or ?k=mediaKey). Prefer url / renderUrl.

WebhookEvent.description: POST to your URL with X-Monkeygun-Event and X-Monkeygun-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw body). One attempt, 15 s timeout, no retry — poll GET /videos/{id} as the fallback.

post.summary: Read a source before cutting from it
post.description: Read a source before cutting from it. Give a URL, library asset ids, or pasted text. Returns a source pack: title, summary, verbatim facts, stills, brand colors/fonts, and an error if the page did not load or had no readable text. Free.

url.description: Public URL to read (page or PDF)

assetIds.description: Library asset ids (images become stills; video/audio become footage/music; PDF/text become text)

text.description: Pasted notes or a script the person gave you

data.description: Structured facts from an API caller (e.g. a token snapshot: symbol, priceUsd, change24hPct, holders…). Every value becomes a quotable fact; numbers are formatted for speech. Optional imageUrl/logoUrl and statsPage inside are used as the still and source link.

summary.description: One-line summary for a data source

imageUrl.description: Logo/hero image URL for a data source

note.description: What they said this source is, if useful

post.summary: Structured numbers from real data APIs — prices, market caps, changes, OHLC, weather, FX
post.description: Structured numbers from real data APIs — prices, market caps, changes, OHLC, weather, FX. Use this INSTEAD of web_search for anything with a number: crypto (CoinGecko), stocks / indices / ETFs (Yahoo), weather (Open-Meteo), currencies (Frankfurter). Free. Returns facts and a sourcePackId ready for create_video.

kind.description: crypto = coins by symbol or name; stock = tickers, indices (^IXIC, ^GSPC), ETFs; weather = a place; fx = currency pairs

symbols.description: e.g. ["BTC","ETH"], ["NVDA","^IXIC"], ["EUR","JPY"] (vs USD unless base given), or a place name for weather

base.description: fx only: base currency, default USD

post.summary: Search the web (titles, urls, snippets) when you need a source you do not have yet — a company page, a news item, a stat
post.description: Search the web (titles, urls, snippets) when you need a source you do not have yet — a company page, a news item, a stat. 2 credits. Follow up with inspect_source on the best result; never quote a snippet as fact.

post.summary: List recently inspected sources (id, title, url, whether it errored)
post.description: List recently inspected sources (id, title, url, whether it errored). Free.

post.summary: Current credit balance and plan for the signed-in account
post.description: Current credit balance and plan for the signed-in account. Free.

post.summary: Price a video before making it
post.description: Price a video before making it. Returns credits and a component breakdown. Free.

images.description: Visuals policy. 'source' = real stills only (default when a source has stills); 'auto' = stills first, generate only where nothing real exists; 'generate' = generated image on every visual scene (25cr each); 'none' = typography only.

clips.description: AI motion clips made from stills on some scenes, billed per second. Only when asked or configured.

provider.description: Per second of footage: minimax (MiniMax H3, 768p) 15cr · kling (1080p) 20cr · seedance-lite (Seedance 2.0 fast) 50cr · seedance-pro (Seedance 2.5, native audio, up to 30s) 100cr

count.description: How many scenes get a clip (1-4)

aiVideo.description: Full AI video: one generated shot for the whole runtime (voice + captions on top). seedance-pro up to 30s; minimax up to 15s. Expensive — quote first.

provider.description: Per second of footage: minimax (MiniMax H3, 768p) 15cr · kling (1080p) 20cr · seedance-lite (Seedance 2.0 fast) 50cr · seedance-pro (Seedance 2.5, native audio, up to 30s) 100cr

withAudio.description: seedance-pro only: generate ambient audio under the voiceover

prompt.description: Visual direction for the footage; default derived from the script

shots.description: Number of shots to stitch. Default: enough to cover the runtime (a 60s MiniMax video = 4 × 15s). Each shot is seeded with the last frame of the previous one.

secondsPerShot.description: Length of each shot (default: the provider maximum — minimax 15, seedance-pro 30, kling 10)

prompts.description: One visual direction per shot, for a story that changes scene

targetSeconds.description: Runtime in seconds — drives script/voice/render units and AI footage cost. Default 30

post.summary: What is saved about this account: brand kit, voices, audiences, CTAs, never-say, preferences, sources
post.description: What is saved about this account: brand kit, voices, audiences, CTAs, never-say, preferences, sources. Free. Usually already in the runtime context.

post.summary: Remember something about them for every future video: brandKit {accent, ground, fonts[], watermark, pack}, audiences[], ctas[], never[], styleNotes, prefs {tier, format, language}, voices[{voiceId,name,kind,default}]
post.description: Remember something about them for every future video: brandKit {accent, ground, fonts[], watermark, pack}, audiences[], ctas[], never[], styleNotes, prefs {tier, format, language}, voices[{voiceId,name,kind,default}]. Also decision: a one-line note of what they told you. Free.

post.summary: Build their brand kit from a site (colors, primary, fonts) and save it on the profile; every later video inherits it
post.description: Build their brand kit from a site (colors, primary, fonts) and save it on the profile; every later video inherits it. Free. Give url or sourcePackId; optional watermark text and pack (classic | editorial | bold | cinematic).

post.summary: Plan before making, when the spend is over ~200 credits, the ask was unformed, or they asked to see a plan: drafts the script (charged as a script), returns storyboard frames (beat · what is on screen · duration), the settings you chose (format, length, tier, voice, visuals), the full cost and the proof cost, and a planId
post.description: Plan before making, when the spend is over ~200 credits, the ask was unformed, or they asked to see a plan: drafts the script (charged as a script), returns storyboard frames (beat · what is on screen · duration), the settings you chose (format, length, tier, voice, visuals), the full cost and the proof cost, and a planId. The web shows it as a card with "Make it" and "Proof first". Pass what you settled: brief, sourcePackId(s), libraryAssetIds, format, targetSeconds, tier, workflow, voiceover, and plan {message, audience, outcome, look, stated[], inferred[]}.

brief.description: The ask in your words: subject, audience, angle, CTA, anything they specified

libraryAssetIds.description: their files to use (a track, footage, images, a logo)

targetSeconds.description: Runtime; music video = the track length automatically

tier.description: fast = stills + motion; standard = 1080p AI clips; cinematic = full AI footage

plan.description: { message, audience, outcome, look, stated: [what they told you], inferred: [what you decided and why] }

post.summary: Render the first ~8 seconds of a plan in its look, voice and tier (one clip at most) so they can judge before the full spend
post.description: Render the first ~8 seconds of a plan in its look, voice and tier (one clip at most) so they can judge before the full spend. Costs the proof price the plan quoted. Returns proofVideoId.

post.summary: Make a video from YOUR script: records the voiceover, places the stills you chose / library media / generated images, optional clips or presenter, times captions
post.description: Make a video from YOUR script: records the voiceover, places the stills you chose / library media / generated images, optional clips or presenter, times captions. Costs credits (quote first for a new video). Returns the video (status "scripted") — call render_video next to produce the MP4.

planId.description: Make the video from a saved plan (after "make it"): the plan's script, settings and files are used; anything else you pass overrides. The script draft is not charged again.

brief.description: What the video is about and for — the ask in your words, including audience, angle, CTA, and anything the person specified

script.description: The script you wrote (see "Writing the script"). Omit only for a quick engine-written first pass.

grounding.description: Exact source phrase this rests on; "" for framing/CTA

stillIndex.description: Index of a source still to show (each at most once)

clipRef.description: A cut from indexed footage (see index_footage): which asset, where to start, how long

imagePrompt.description: Generated image prompt — only when images allow generation and no real still fits

frame.description: Show this scene's image inside a device: phone for app screens, laptop for websites and dashboards, card for a plain screenshot. Use on almost every screenshot beat.

stats.description: Stat pills for a data scene instead of one figure, e.g. [{value:"84.6k",label:"stars"},{value:"448",label:"forks"}] (2–4)

transition.description: How this scene hands off to the next: wipe (accent bar sweep, the pack default), cut (hard cut), dissolve (this scene fades out, the next fades in). Mix them: dissolve into a mood shot, cut into a stat, wipe into the CTA.

sfx.description: Sound effect on this scene: 'impact' | 'whoosh' | 'riser' | 'tick' | 'keys' | 'none', or { assetId } for your own library audio (generate_sfx lands one there; optional volume 0–1). Omit for the pack's automatic pick.

chart.description: chart scenes: a real chart drawn from your numbers. line = draw-on with glowing endpoint and the last value labeled; bars = grow-in, accent above the baseline / negativeColor below, value labels. text = the title above it.

series.description: number[] or [{ t: label, v: number }] in order (2–60 points; bars ≤ 12)

labels.description: x labels (bars: one per bar; line: first/last shown)

color.description: hex; default accent (line: red-ish when the series ends lower)

negativeColor.description: hex for values below the baseline

baseline.description: bars: 0 (zero line, negatives hang down) or 'min' (default when all values are positive)

title.description: small caption under the chart: source, window

motion.description: How the scene moves. Default is picked per type (title→kinetic, data→countup, visual→slide/zoom, quote→typewriter); slam = hit-in with a shake for a hero number or word; set it to change rhythm.

asset.description: Media for this scene: a public http(s) image or mp4 url (fetched at create time, full-bleed under the text, videos muted) or a library file path

kind.description: inferred from the file when omitted

mediaStart.description: video: seconds into the file to start

clipPrompt.description: Motion description for an AI clip — only when clips are enabled

sourcePackId.description: From inspect_source. Omit only for a deliberately ungrounded topic video.

sourcePackIds.description: Several sources at once (multi-link briefs, market_data + a page) — merged into one grounded pack

lyrics.description: music-video only: the lyrics to show on screen, one line per scene in order. Leave out for a pure visual (default).

tier.description: Quality tier you told them: fast = stills + motion; standard = 1080p AI clips (kling); cinematic = full AI footage (seedance-pro). Picks the clip model when clips has no provider.

plan.description: The brief you settled on, saved on the video: { message, audience, outcome, look, stated: [what they told you], inferred: [what you decided and why] }

workflow.description: Composition approach. music-video for a person's own track (no VO, no captions, no SFX, no on-screen text unless lyrics; runtime = the track); product-launch for a company/site/product page; faceless-explainer for an article/notes; talking-head when a presenter is used; motion-graphics for a short unnarrated stat hit.

images.description: Visuals policy. 'source' = real stills only (default when a source has stills); 'auto' = stills first, generate only where nothing real exists; 'generate' = generated image on every visual scene (25cr each); 'none' = typography only.

clips.description: AI motion clips made from stills on some scenes, billed per second. Only when asked or configured.

provider.description: Per second of footage: minimax (MiniMax H3, 768p) 15cr · kling (1080p) 20cr · seedance-lite (Seedance 2.0 fast) 50cr · seedance-pro (Seedance 2.5, native audio, up to 30s) 100cr

count.description: How many scenes get a clip (1-4)

aiVideo.description: Full AI video: one generated shot for the whole runtime (voice + captions on top). seedance-pro up to 30s; minimax up to 15s. Expensive — quote first.

provider.description: Per second of footage: minimax (MiniMax H3, 768p) 15cr · kling (1080p) 20cr · seedance-lite (Seedance 2.0 fast) 50cr · seedance-pro (Seedance 2.5, native audio, up to 30s) 100cr

withAudio.description: seedance-pro only: generate ambient audio under the voiceover

prompt.description: Visual direction for the footage; default derived from the script

shots.description: Number of shots to stitch. Default: enough to cover the runtime (a 60s MiniMax video = 4 × 15s). Each shot is seeded with the last frame of the previous one.

secondsPerShot.description: Length of each shot (default: the provider maximum — minimax 15, seedance-pro 30, kling 10)

prompts.description: One visual direction per shot, for a story that changes scene

avatar.description: A talking presenter lip-synced to the voiceover. Per second of runtime: stock 3cr/s, photo 25cr/s.

mode.description: 'photo' animates a library photo with a clear face; 'stock' uses a stock presenter

imageAssetId.description: photo mode: library asset id of the face photo

avatarId.description: stock mode: presenter id or a hint like 'emily', 'marcus', 'any_female'. Vertical presenters are picked automatically for 9:16 / 4:5.

public.description: true = the finished file is playable without a key (share links, feeds). Default false: media needs the keyed url / mediaKey returned with the video.

layout.description: 'split' = the presenter (avatar or their footage) fills the bottom third while your scenes/motion graphics play in the top two-thirds — the talking-head-with-changing-content format. Needs avatar or footage. Default 'full'.

captions.description: Timed captions from the voiceover. Default true.

voiceId.description: Voice for the voiceover (a show's configured voice, or a cloned voice id the person owns). Default: house voice.

language.description: Language for narration and on-screen text (e.g. "Spanish", "pt-BR", "Japanese"). Default English / the source language.

voiceover.description: false = silent piece (no narration, no captions). Default true; auto-false under 3s.

targetSeconds.description: Target runtime in seconds — anything from 1 to long form (a 10-minute episode = 600). Default follows the source (25-40s). Cost scales with it.

pacing.description: Scene density: calm ≈ 9s scenes (documentary), standard ≈ 6s, fast ≈ 3.5s (roast, hype). Default standard, or the show's setting.

libraryAssetIds.description: Library assets to place: images/videos go on visual scenes, an audio file becomes the music bed

brand.description: Override brand tokens (otherwise taken from the source page)

pack.description: Style pack: one coherent look — editorial (serif, warm, slow), bold (condensed uppercase, hot accent, fast), cinematic (letterbox, filmic grade, slow push-ins), classic (default). Sets fonts, palette, motion, grade and sound design; explicit brand fields still win.

watermark.description: Small corner text; empty string removes it

disclaimer.description: Required legal line shown for the whole video, exactly as given

channelId.description: Make it as an episode of this channel

post.summary: Produce the MP4 for a video (10cr)
post.description: Produce the MP4 for a video (10cr). Runs the quality check first; on failure returns the problems so you can fix and retry. Takes 1-3 minutes; progress streams to the person. If it returns an error (including "Already rendering"), no new cut exists — say exactly that; never tell the person it rendered.

post.summary: Apply a typed edit to an existing video: shorter, new hook, different CTA, drop a scene, lead with the price, tone
post.description: Apply a typed edit to an existing video: shorter, new hook, different CTA, drop a scene, lead with the price, tone. Pass the person's words and your revised script (get_video shows the current one); keep stillIndex on scenes whose picture should stay. Keeps source, brand, voice; re-records voice only if the words changed; re-times captions. 20-50cr (scales with length). Then render_video.

notes.description: The person's edit verbatim, plus your concrete reading of it

post.description: Make another language version of an existing video: narration, on-screen text, title and CTA translated (names, brands, figures unchanged), voice re-recorded, captions re-timed, same stills and brand. Costs like an edit with a new voice (scales with length). Then render_video.

post.description: A fresh take on the same source: new angle, new script, same brand/format/options. Costs like a new video. Then render_video.

videoId.description: The video to take another swing at

angle.description: What should be different this time

post.summary: Reorder or drop scenes without touching their content: pass the new order as 1-based scene numbers (omit a number to cut that scene)
post.description: Reorder or drop scenes without touching their content: pass the new order as 1-based scene numbers (omit a number to cut that scene). Free; render to see it. The voiceover is not re-recorded, so only use it when the narration order still makes sense — otherwise edit_video.

post.summary: Edit one scene without touching the rest: its on-screen text, type, duration, or image prompt
post.description: Edit one scene without touching the rest: its on-screen text, type, duration, or image prompt. Free; then render_video.

One call: structured data → source → video → render → webhook
post.description: For system integrations (e.g. a token page, a listing, a filing). Every value in `data` becomes a quotable fact. Returns 202 while rendering; `video.rendered` arrives on your webhook. Creation with `clips`/`aiVideo` can take minutes — pass `pacing` (calm | standard | fast) for scene density; pass `async: true` to get 202 + `jobId` immediately, then poll `GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}` (videoId appears once the script/voice/images exist) or listen for `video.created`.

data.description: Your structured facts (symbol, priceUsd, change24hPct, holders, …). Optional: omit for a creative brief-driven video.

public.description: Finished file playable without a key. Otherwise use the keyed url / renderUrl / mediaKey returned on the video, the job, and the webhook.

post.summary: Mint a studio session for one of your users (white-label embed)
post.description: Iframe the returned `url` (https://monkeygun.com/embed/studio#t=…). The studio runs on your account for billing and ownership; every video and chat is tagged with `externalUserId`, and the page posts `{ type: "monkeygun", event: "video.created" | "video.rendered", videoId, url }` to the parent window. Rendered-video webhooks carry `externalUserId` too. TTL 5 minutes to 7 days (default 12 h).

brand.description: Brand lock forced on everything made in this session
